title: Inverse image along an isomorphism of schemes on the pro-etale site
statement:
Let $g:X\to Y$ be an isomorphism of schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], with small pro-etale sites $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$, $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and let $g^{-1}$, $g_*$ and the structure maps $c^g_A:g^{-1}A_Y\to A_X$ be the inverse image, direct image and structure maps of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Then:

1. The functor $\Phi_g:X_{\mathrm{proet}}\to Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$, $(U\xrightarrow{u}X)\mapsto(U\xrightarrow{g\circ u}Y)$, is an equivalence of categories, with quasi-inverse $(V\xrightarrow{v}Y)\mapsto(V\xrightarrow{g^{-1}\circ v}X)$; both functors send coverings to coverings. For every sheaf $\mathcal F$ on $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$ there is an isomorphism $(g^{-1}\mathcal F)(U\xrightarrow{u}X)\cong\mathcal F(U\xrightarrow{g\circ u}Y)$, natural in $\mathcal F$ and in $U$.
2. $g^{-1}$ is an equivalence of categories from sheaves on $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$ to sheaves on $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ (of sets, abelian groups, rings, or modules over a constant sheaf of rings), with quasi-inverse $g_*$. In particular $g^{-1}$ is exact and commutes with all small limits and colimits; for every inverse system $(\mathcal F_n)_{n\geq1}$ of sheaves on $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$ the canonical map $g^{-1}\varprojlim_n\mathcal F_n\to\varprojlim_ng^{-1}\mathcal F_n$ [def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit], induced by the inverse images of the projections, is an isomorphism.
3. For every commutative ring $A$ the structure map $c^g_A:g^{-1}A_Y\to A_X$ is an isomorphism of sheaves of rings, and for every ring homomorphism $\varphi:A\to B$, with $\varphi_Y:A_Y\to B_Y$ and $\varphi_X:A_X\to B_X$ the induced maps of constant sheaves, $\varphi_X\circ c^g_A=c^g_B\circ g^{-1}(\varphi_Y)$.
